title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page continues the 'Scholie' of p.60, which axiomatizes the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space. The data are a Hausdorff space Σ and a space Σ*(1) whose points are pairs (x<y). It carries two maps: b (target, y), a proper 'boundary immersion' (immersion bordante), and s = p1 (source, x). Σ*(2) is the space of chains (x<y<z), with p2:(x<y<z)↦(x,y), s':↦(x,z) and b':↦(y,z). Geometrically, Σ should be the disjoint union of the resolved (unfolded) strata. b embeds the boundary faces of a resolved stratum into it. s projects a boundary face onto the resolved closure of a lower stratum. The order x<y means 'y lies on a boundary face fibred over x'. This is a manifold-with-fibred-corners / iterated-fibration structure.

Condition 3b (this page): the map Σ*(2)→Σ×Σ, (x<y<z)↦(x,z), factors through (p1,b): Σ*(1)→Σ×Σ. This is transitivity: there is a composition map Σ*(2)→Σ*(1). The square with b':Σ*(2)→Σ*(1), p2:Σ*(2)→Σ*(1), b:Σ*(1)→Σ and p1:Σ*(1)→Σ is required to be cartesian. Thus Σ*(2) ≅ Σ*(1)×_{b,Σ,p1}Σ*(1): the space of chains equals the space of composable pairs, a Segal-type condition for the nerve of a topological poset. In addition, p1 must be transversal to the boundary immersion b, so the fibre product is again a nice 'bordant' object (corners of higher codimension).

Marginal NB: if Σ is Hausdorff (so Σ×Σ is Hausdorff) and b is proper, then (s,b):Σ*(1)→Σ×Σ is proper, since its second component b is proper and the target is separated. Being injective (condition 3a), it is then a closed embedding.

He then starts an 'equivalent' reformulation, entirely in terms of one Hausdorff space Σ with an order relation x≼y. The conditions are: Σ_{<x} is finite and (totally) ordered; the graph Σ*(1) of the strict order has a proper boundary-immersion target map b; and the germs at x of the images under b of the (Σ*(1),z_α), for z_α over x, form a transversal family of boundary subspaces. These conditions are crossed out here and redone on p.61's successor (p.27 of his numbering). So the whole unfolded stratified structure is encoded as a topological poset whose nerve Σ*(•) is built from boundary immersions. The original stratified space would presumably be recovered by collapsing along s.
errors: Labelling slip: the morphism obtained by factoring (p1∘s', b∘b') = (x,z) through (p1,b) is the composition (x<y<z)↦(x<z), which on p.60 is called s', not p2. p2 (↦(x,y)) is rather the left arrow of the cartesian square. Writing 'en un morphisme p2' conflates the two; the intended mathematics is clear.
The NB tacitly needs (s,b) injective (condition 3a) to conclude 'plongement fermé'. Properness alone gives only a closed map; the argument is otherwise correct.

Total order on Σ_{<x} is asserted in the struck draft; the next page weakens this to 'fini ordonné'. Which is right depends on whether boundary faces through a corner are totally ordered, as in a flag of strata. The draft is unsettled.

ideas.what: Encoding the unfolding of a stratified space as a space Σ (union of resolved strata) with a proper boundary immersion b and source/projection map s from the face space Σ*(1)
ideas.modern_name: manifold with fibred corners / iterated fibration structure / resolution (unzipping) of a Thom–Mather or conically smooth stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data; Verona (1984); Melrose and Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017, 'unzipping')
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 discusses 'déploiement' of stratified structures, only in outline

ideas.what: Cartesian square Σ*(2) = Σ*(1)×_Σ Σ*(1) plus composition map: the face data form the nerve of a topological poset satisfying a Segal-type condition
ideas.modern_name: topological category / Segal space (nerve of a topological poset), exit-path-like category of resolved strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal (1968/74) for the nerve condition; Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for exit-path ∞-categories of stratified spaces

ideas.what: Transversality of the source map s to the boundary immersion b, so that corners of higher codimension arise as fibre products
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of boundary fibrations at corners (iterated fibration structure axiom)

missed.claim: Grothendieck reformulates the unfolded (fibred-corner) structure of a stratified space as a single Hausdorff space with a topological order relation. The relation's graph and space of chains form a nerve with a cartesian (Segal) square and proper boundary-immersion face maps. This point-level 'topological poset of resolved strata' sits between the analysts' iterated fibration structures (Melrose, ALMP) and the homotopy theorists' exit-path categories (Lurie, AFT). That bridge is made only implicitly in later literature.
missed.quote: De façon équivalente, une telle structure est donnée par un espace topologique séparé Σ, relation d'ordre x ≼ y satisfaisant aux conditions suivantes
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a strict, point-set model of a stratified space's resolution as a topological category. This could give a direct comparison between manifolds with fibred corners and the exit-path ∞-category, without passing through conically smooth atlases.

missed.claim: The equivalence between the 'Scholie' data (Σ, Σ*(1), Σ*(2), s, b with cartesian square and transversality) and the order-relation formulation is stated but not proved. The draft conditions are crossed out and only partially rewritten on the next page.
missed.quote: a) Si x ∈ Σ, Σ_{<x} est un ensemble (fini) totalement ordonné
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A precise theorem of this kind (topological posets with transversal proper boundary immersions ≅ unfolded stratified spaces) does not seem to be stated in this form in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The déploiement idea itself is announced in the Esquisse and corresponds to well-known later notions (fibred corners, unzipping). The specific encoding as a topological order relation with a Segal-type cartesian square is a notable unpublished detail, but it is a draft and close in spirit to later work.
transcription_corrections: The factorization in condition b) should be read as (p1∘s', b∘b'), i.e. (x,z); the transcription's '[-p b-] b'' is a correction of 'pb' to 'b''. The factored morphism is the composition s', despite the written 'p2'.
Marginal NB reads approximately: 'NB Si Σ est séparé, donc Σ×Σ séparé, et Σ*(1) →b Σ propre, il en résulte que Σ*(1) → Σ×Σ est propre donc un plongement fermé' rather than 'Σ séparé sur Σ'.
Second margin, approximately: 'cette condition de transversalité est garantie par la condition de [?] (connexité?) ...', which remains largely illegible.
Struck lines include '(= Σ*(1)_x)' and 'a) Si x ∈ Σ, Σ_{<x} est un ensemble (fini) totalement ordonné'. 'immersion bordante propre' is the intended phrase.
